name: Hopline
tagline: Chat with everyone around you when there's no signal
description:
Hopline is group chat for places with no mobile signal and no WiFi: treks, camps, festivals, fairs, rallies, power cuts.

Phones link to each other directly over Bluetooth and WiFi, and every phone passes messages along for the others. A message can travel down a whole line of hikers or across a packed ground, far beyond the reach of any single phone. No internet, no account, no server, no hotspot to set up.

One person starts a group and gets a 3-word code like "tiger river lamp". Everyone else types the three words or scans the QR. Then it's a familiar chat app: one group chat, private chats, photos and small files. Walk out of range and back, and the chat catches up by itself.

Photos are shrunk hard (about 0.3 MB) so they hop in seconds, travel phone to phone in pieces, and are put back together on every phone - even ones that were away when you sent them. Files up to 2 MB. Keep more than one group - the trek, the family, the festival crew - and switch with a tap; each keeps its own history, unread counts and photos.

The ticks never lie: a clock while it waits for a phone in range, one tick when it's on its way, two ticks when phones confirm. A photo's tick only appears when the whole photo is on the other phone. Tap your own message to see exactly who has it, by name.

Built for a few friends or a crowd: in a small group every phone confirms every message; in a gathering of hundreds the phones automatically stop chattering about receipts, slow their "I'm here" beacons and switch photos off, so the radios carry your words instead of overhead.

If anyone in the group gets internet, everyone can use a sliver of it: read a web page as plain text, or send an SMS/email home through the friend's phone - the answer hops back to the whole group. Your phone only shares while its "Share my internet" switch is on.

Android 8+ with Google Play services. Each hop is Bluetooth range (about 20-40 m in the open). Android only; no end-to-end encryption; media kept deliberately small. Install it on every phone before you need it.
